external/github.txt

WHAT THIS IS
  Our two GitHub repositories and how we use branches in them.
  Repo 1 = this folder (Calhacks/): the tool, and our Devpost submission. It must be public before
           we submit; Devpost wants a repo "for any code to be considered".
  Repo 2 = demo-app/: the small app the agents edit in the demo. It has its own git history, and
           repo 1's .gitignore excludes the folder.

WHO / WHEN
  C creates both tonight. Everyone gets write access to both.

STEPS
  1. Create both repos on GitHub. Private is fine until Sunday morning; make repo 1 (and 2) public
     before submitting.
  2. Repo 1: git init in Calhacks/, first commit, push. Check that .env is NOT in the commit.
  3. Repo 2: git init in demo-app/, commit the baseline (typecheck and tests green), push main, then:
       git tag demo-base
       git push origin demo-base
     scripts/demo-reset.ts --reset-main moves main back to this tag before every rehearsal.
  4. Add all four of us as collaborators with write access.

BRANCHES IN REPO 2
  main            the shared code. People commit and push here as usual.
  wip/<name>      written ONLY by the hooks: a force-pushed snapshot of that person's uncommitted
                  work. Never commit to it by hand and never merge it into main. demo-reset.ts deletes them.
  demo-base       a tag on the baseline commit of the scripted demo.

ACCESS FROM THE HOOKS
  The hooks push from each laptop with that laptop's normal git credentials. If `git push` works in
  your clone, the hooks can push too. The orchestrator's laptop only needs read access.
